card.changed: Chained hops no longer stack speed without limit. A jump from a roll flies exactly as before; past top speed its lean forward fades smoothly, and a landing soaks up some of the speed past top speed. The best hopping rhythm is now about one and a half times as fast as rolling, where it was nearly three times.
try: Roll right through the hills and along the flat (hold right).
Press R, then do the same stretch hopping: tap jump over and over while holding right.
Jump the gaps and the lava as you normally would.
lookFor: Whether hopping still feels worth it, but not the only way to move, on the flat and over the hills.
Whether landings after fast hops feel like a brake or a stumble.
Whether a long-charged jump from a full roll feels shorter or floatier than before.
known: Measured over 8 s from the start (`node prototypes/03-bot-search/src/speed.ts`): rolling 445 cells; hopping every 20 frames 664 (it was 1118). The fastest rhythm found, 714 (it was about 1400).
Over the hills, hopping is still about twice as fast as rolling (it was four times): rolling uphill is slow.
A jump from faster than top speed leans forward a little less: rolling downhill, or a long wind-up while rolling (he speeds up as he squashes). Those land a few cells shorter and a little higher.
A landing after fast hops takes the extra speed in one frame.
questions: Is hopping slowed the right amount: too little, right, or too much?
Do single jumps feel the same as before?
